$comment: Baseball leagues. Add one by appending an entry — nothing in the model or API hardcodes these ids. `oddsSportKeys` are The Odds API sport keys (upcoming games + bookmaker prices). `retrosheet` marks the leagues with a real results feed; a league without one still shows upcoming games and MARKET probabilities, and the UI says so rather than inventing a model. Only MLB has an open, game-by-game public archive — NPB and KBO simply do not, and pretending otherwise would be worse than admitting it.

history.$comment: Seasons of results to ingest by default. Baseball rosters turn over slowly and a season is 2,430 games, so eight seasons is already ~19k games — more than enough for stable ratings, and the ingest stays under a couple of minutes.
history.$comment_retrosheet: Retrosheet event files mirrored on GitHub by the Chadwick Baseball Bureau. One file per team per season holding that team's HOME games, so 30 files cover a season exactly once. They carry the starting pitchers — which is the single most important fact about a baseball game — but not the final score, which is counted off the plays. See docs/BASEBALL.md for how that parser was validated.
history.$comment_gamelog: Retrosheet's own game logs, which DO carry official final scores. Used to verify the event parser rather than as a data source: gl2011 is the file the parser was checked against, game by game.
history.$comment_probables: MLB's own public Stats API — no key, no rate limit worth worrying about. It is where tomorrow's ANNOUNCED STARTING PITCHERS come from, which is what makes a same-day forecast worth anything. Blocked in the environment this was built in; see the docs.
